# Watching an HTTP location and sending only what changed

The bundled `sensor-http` service polls a URL and sends a message when the
response body changes. The watch is declared as a publisher entry on the
template; no publisher of your own is needed.

## Wire the sensor

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers: {}
named_locks: {}
executors: {}
publishers:
  "watch":
    endpoint: "http-sensor:9082"
    protocols: ["publisher"]
  "watch-filtered":
    endpoint: "http-sensor:9082"
    protocols: ["publisher"]
```

```bash
docker run -d --network rimsky-net --network-alias http-sensor \
  -e RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL=http://rimsky:8080 \
  -e RIMSKY_SENSOR_HTTP_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST=172.31.0.0/16 \
  -e RIMSKY_SENSOR_HTTP_STATE_DSN='postgres://...' \
  rimsky-sensor-http:<tag>
```

## The template

```json
{
  "name": "sensor-http-demo",
  "version": "1",
  "messages": [{"type": "http/obs"}, {"type": "http/filtered"}],
  "nodes": [{
    "type": "reactor",
    "kind": "attribute_passthrough",
    "subscribes": [{"node": "http/obs", "type": "terminal/success",
                    "force_upstream_refresh": false}],
    "attributes": {"schema": {"type": "object",
                              "properties": {"v": {"type": "integer", "default": 1}}}}
  }],
  "publishers": [
    {"name": "watch", "kind": "http", "message_type": "http/obs",
     "config": {"url": "http://poll-target:8000/data.json", "poll_interval": "1s"}},
    {"name": "watch-filtered", "kind": "http", "message_type": "http/filtered",
     "config": {"url": "http://poll-target:8000/data.json", "poll_interval": "1s",
                "match": {"jsonpath": {"path": "status", "value": "ready"}}}}
  ]
}
```

## Poll and send on change

The unfiltered watch sends a message carrying the response status, the URL, the
decoded body and a hash of that body. The subscribed node runs on it.

Rewrite the document and a second message arrives, carrying the new body and a
different hash. The change is what sends.

A watch on a location that never answers with success sends nothing: an
unsuccessful poll is not a message.

## An unchanged body stays quiet, across a restart

Leave the document alone and create a second instance. Its own first message
shows the poller is still running — and across that, the first instance stays at
exactly the messages it already had.

Restart the sensor container and create a third instance. Its watch sends its
first message while the first instance still holds exactly the same count. The
last-seen body survives the restart, so restarting the sensor does not replay
the whole watch into the graph.

## Narrow a watch with a filter

The `match` config narrows what becomes a message. Across three successive
bodies, the filtered watch sends exactly one — the body satisfying its declared
match — while the unfiltered watch on the same URL has sent all three.

The filter composes with the change detection rather than replacing it.

## Private targets are refused until you open the range

Run a second sensor with no `RIMSKY_SENSOR_HTTP_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST` and route a
watch to it. It sends nothing across the whole run, and its log records the
refused dial.

An operator reaches an internal location only by naming its range. A watch that
names a private target on an unconfigured sensor fails visibly rather than
silently succeeding.
